title: feat: add Azure GPT transcription models
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds `gpt-transcribe` to `/v1/audio/transcriptions` through the Sweden Central Azure deployment.
- Adds `gpt-live-transcribe` to `/realtime` and `/v1/realtime`, preserving the public model ID while mapping Azure's internal deployment name.
- Makes both models Quest-Pollen-accessible with the confirmed `0.75` Azure multiplier and provisional OpenAI list costs of `$0.0045/min` and `$0.017/min`.
- Bills Azure's duration usage exactly and fails closed when batch or realtime duration metering is missing.

Validation:
- Direct Azure batch probe: 60 seconds, HTTP 200, exact `gpt-transcribe-2026-07-28`, duration usage present.
- Direct Azure realtime probe: 3 seconds, completed transcript, duration usage present.
- `npx vitest run test/azure-transcription.test.ts test/realtime.test.ts test/index.test.ts` (103 passed).
- `npm run typecheck`.

Known launch constraint: each Azure deployment currently permits 1 request per minute. Azure's exact cost meters are still pending, so registry costs intentionally use the approved OpenAI prices and can be adjusted later.

gist.headline: The hive has ears
gist.blurb: Two new transcription workers joined the garden: one for recorded audio, one for live conversation. They count every second properly, because bees are surprisingly strict accountants.
gist.summary: Added Azure Sweden Central-backed `gpt-transcribe` to `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `gpt-live-transcribe` to `/realtime` and `/v1/realtime`, with duration-based billing at provisional OpenAI list prices of $0.0045/min and $0.017/min.
gist.impact: Developers can now transcribe uploaded audio or live sessions through the existing public model IDs, while Azure-reported batch and realtime durations are metered exactly for Quest-Pollen access.

Lime-green waveform vines and code-plants show the audio flowing through the new Azure transcription routes, with a small clock emphasizing precise duration metering.
